# Keygen

Keygen is a JSON HTTP API for software licensing, machine activation, entitlements, usage tracking, offline licensing, webhooks, and secure software distribution.

Use this file as a compact map. For implementation details, examples, schemas, request bodies, permissions, authentication rules, response bodies, and error cases, open the linked docs.

Base API URL: `https://api.keygen.sh/v1/accounts/<account>` where `<account>` is an account UUID or slug.

Core rules:

- Always use TLS
- Send JSON unless the endpoint specifies otherwise (rare)
- Treat license validation responses as structured data, and inspect the response not HTTP status codes for the validation result
- Use `Authorization: License <key>` for client-side integrations, and `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when required server-side
- Do not expose admin, environment, or product tokens in client software

## Essential Guides

Start here when choosing an integration path, licensing model, or implementation workflow before opening individual API resource docs.

- [API reference](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/): Complete API reference for resources, schemas, endpoints, examples, authentication, and permissions.
- [Your account](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/#your-keygen-account): Explains account IDs/slugs and protected vs unprotected account behavior.
- [Content types](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/#jsonapi): Use when setting `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers for JSON and JSON:API requests.
- [Client libraries](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/#client-libraries): Use when deciding between SDKs, community libraries, and raw HTTP clients.
- [Getting started](https://keygen.sh/docs/getting-started/): First-stop guide for a new Keygen API integration.
- [Choosing a licensing model](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/): Use when deciding how licenses should be enforced.
- [Perpetual licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/perpetual-licenses/): Use for licenses that grant indefinite access.
- [Timed licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/timed-licenses/): Use for subscriptions, trials, or licenses with expiration.
- [Floating licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/floating-licenses/): Use when seats can move between multiple machines.
- [Node-locked licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/node-locked-licenses/): Use when access should be bound to specific machine fingerprints.
- [User-locked licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/user-locked-licenses/): Use when access should be bound to an authenticated user.
- [Feature licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/feature-licenses/): Use when individual product features are controlled by entitlements.
- [Metered licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/metered-licenses/): Use when access is limited by counted usage.
- [Offline licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/choosing-a-licensing-model/offline-licenses/): Use when software must validate licenses without network access.
- [Validating license keys](https://keygen.sh/docs/validating-licenses/): Use when implementing license-key validation in an app.
- [Activating devices](https://keygen.sh/docs/activating-machines/): Use when implementing machine activation for node-locked or floating licenses.
- [Storing metadata](https://keygen.sh/docs/storing-metadata/): Use when attaching custom structured data to Keygen resources.
- [Using webhooks](https://keygen.sh/docs/using-webhooks/): Use when syncing Keygen events to billing, provisioning, or backend workflows.
- [Keygen Relay](https://keygen.sh/docs/relay/): Use when proxying Keygen API traffic through Relay.
- [Keygen CLI](https://keygen.sh/docs/cli/): Use for command-line release, package, and distribution workflows.
- [Custom domains](https://keygen.sh/docs/custom-domains/): Use when serving Keygen-backed endpoints through a custom domain.
- [SAML/SSO](https://keygen.sh/docs/sso/): Use when configuring single sign-on.
- [Static IPs](https://keygen.sh/docs/static-ips/): Use when network policy requires stable IP allowlisting.
- [Self hosting](https://keygen.sh/docs/self-hosting/): Use when evaluating or operating a self-hosted Keygen deployment.
- [Searching](https://keygen.sh/docs/search/): Use when querying resources with search syntax.
- [Zapier](https://keygen.sh/docs/zapier/): Use when automating Keygen workflows with Zapier.

- [Sandbox](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/sandbox/): Use when working in a non-production sandbox.

## Licensing Resources

These resources model the core licensing system: products, policies, users, licenses, machines, entitlements, and the tokens that authorize access.

### API Tokens

Tokens authenticate API calls. Use these docs when issuing, rotating, revoking, or listing credentials for accounts, products, users, licenses, or environments.

- [API Tokens](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/): Overview of token authentication and token lifecycle.
- [Token object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-object): Use when reading token attributes and relationships.
- [Generate a token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-generate): Use when creating a new credential.
- [Retrieve a token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-retrieve): Use when fetching token metadata.
- [Regenerate a token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-regenerate): Use when rotating an existing token.
- [Revoke a token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-revoke): Use when invalidating a credential.
- [List all tokens](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/tokens/#tokens-list): Use when auditing or displaying tokens.

### Environments

Environments isolate resources and credentials. Use them to separate production, staging, testing, or tenant-specific API contexts.

- [Environments](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/): Overview of environment isolation.
- [Environment object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-object): Use when reading environment fields.
- [Create an environment](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-create): Use when adding a new isolated context.
- [Retrieve an environment](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-retrieve): Use when fetching one environment.
- [Update an environment](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-update): Use when changing environment metadata or settings.
- [Delete an environment](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-delete): Use when removing an environment.
- [List all environments](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-list): Use when showing or auditing environments.
- [Environment tokens](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/environments/#environments-tokens): Use when generating environment-scoped credentials.

### Products

Products represent the software being licensed and distributed. Use products as the parent concept for policies, licenses, releases, and packages.

- [Products](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/): Overview of product resources.
- [Product object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-object): Use when reading product fields and relationships.
- [Create a product](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-create): Use when onboarding a new software product.
- [Retrieve a product](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-retrieve): Use when fetching one product.
- [Update a product](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-update): Use when changing product metadata or settings.
- [Delete a product](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-delete): Use when removing a product.
- [List all products](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-list): Use when displaying all products in an account.
- [Product tokens](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/products/#products-tokens): Use when generating product-scoped credentials.

### Entitlements

Entitlements model features, editions, modules, or capabilities. Use them for feature licensing and release constraints.

- [Entitlements](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/): Overview of entitlement resources.
- [Entitlement object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-object): Use when reading entitlement fields.
- [Create an entitlement](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-create): Use when defining a new feature or capability.
- [Retrieve an entitlement](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-retrieve): Use when fetching one entitlement.
- [Update an entitlement](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-update): Use when renaming or changing entitlement metadata.
- [Delete an entitlement](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-delete): Use when removing a feature or capability.
- [List all entitlements](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/entitlements/#entitlements-list): Use when displaying available features or capabilities.

### Groups

Groups organize users, licenses, or machines. Use them for customer teams, organizations, tenants, or grouped access control.

- [Groups](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/): Overview of group resources.
- [Group object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-object): Use when reading group fields.
- [Create a group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-create): Use when creating a team, tenant, or organization.
- [Retrieve a group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-retrieve): Use when fetching one group.
- [Update a group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-update): Use when changing group details.
- [Delete a group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-delete): Use when removing a group.
- [List all groups](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/groups/#groups-list): Use when displaying or auditing groups.

### Keys

Keys represent key resources. Use these docs when managing explicit key resources rather than using the license key lifecycle directly.

- [Keys](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/): Overview of key resources.
- [Key object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-object): Use when reading key fields.
- [Create a key](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-create): Use when creating a key resource.
- [Retrieve a key](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-retrieve): Use when fetching one key.
- [Update a key](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-update): Use when changing key metadata or settings.
- [Delete a key](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-delete): Use when removing a key.
- [List all keys](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/keys/#keys-list): Use when displaying or auditing keys.

### Policies

Policies define how licenses behave. Use them to configure expiration, machine limits, floating seats, strict validation, heartbeats, usage limits, and entitlement rules.

- [Policies](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/): Overview of license policy resources.
- [Policy object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-object): Use when reading policy rules and limits.
- [Create a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-create): Use when defining a new licensing model.
- [Retrieve a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-retrieve): Use when fetching one policy.
- [Update a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-update): Use when changing license enforcement rules.
- [Delete a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-delete): Use when removing a policy.
- [List all policies](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-list): Use when displaying available license plans.
- [Policy pool](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-pool): Use when popping pre-generated keys from a policy pool.
- [Policy relationships](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-relationships): Use when managing associations for a policy.
- [Attach entitlements to a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-relationships-attach-entitlements): Use when granting features to licenses created under a policy.
- [Detach entitlements from a policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-relationships-detach-entitlements): Use when removing policy-level feature access.
- [List policy entitlements](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/policies/#policies-relationships-list-entitlements): Use when inspecting features attached to a policy.

### Users

Users represent customers or end users. Use them for user authentication, ownership, account access, and user-locked licensing.

- [Users](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/): Overview of user resources.
- [User object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-object): Use when reading user fields and relationships.
- [Create a user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-create): Use when registering or provisioning a user.
- [Retrieve a user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-retrieve): Use when fetching one user.
- [Update a user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-update): Use when changing user details.
- [Delete a user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-delete): Use when removing a user.
- [List all users](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-list): Use when displaying or auditing users.
- [User actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-actions): Use for operations that affect user state.
- [Update password](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-actions-update-password): Use when an authenticated user changes a password.
- [Reset password](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-actions-reset-password): Use when resetting a forgotten password.
- [Ban user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-actions-ban): Use when blocking a user from access.
- [Unban user](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-actions-unban): Use when restoring a banned user's access.
- [User relationships](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-relationships): Use when managing user associations.
- [Generate user token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-tokens): Use when authenticating a user via token.
- [Change user group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#users-relationships-change-group): Use when moving a user between groups.

### Licenses

Licenses are the primary access-granting resources. Use them to issue keys, track state, validate access, attach features/users, and enforce policy rules.

- [Licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/): Overview of license resources.
- [License object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-object): Use when reading license fields, state, and relationships.
- [Create a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-create): Use when issuing a new license.
- [Retrieve a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-retrieve): Use when fetching one license.
- [Update a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-update): Use when changing license metadata or state.
- [Delete a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-delete): Use when removing a license.
- [List all licenses](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-list): Use when displaying or auditing licenses.
- [License actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions): Use for validation, lifecycle, check-out, check-in, and usage operations.
- [Validate by license ID](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-validate): Use when validating a known license resource.
- [Validate by key](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-validate-key): Use when an app submits a license key for validation.
- [Suspend license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-suspend): Use when temporarily disabling a license.
- [Reinstate license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-reinstate): Use when restoring a suspended license.
- [Renew license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-renew): Use when extending a license period.
- [Revoke license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-revoke): Use when permanently invalidating a license.
- [Check out license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-check-out): Use when generating a license file certificate snapshot for offline or air-gapped licensing.
- [Check in license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-check-in): Use when updating a license's check-in timestamps for policies that require periodic check-ins.
- [Increment usage](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-increment-usage): Use when counting metered consumption.
- [Decrement usage](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-decrement-usage): Use when reversing or reducing metered consumption.
- [Reset usage](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-actions-reset-usage): Use when clearing metered usage.
- [License relationships](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships): Use when managing license associations.
- [Generate license token](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-activation-tokens): Use when granting a license-scoped credential.
- [Attach entitlements to a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-attach-entitlements): Use when granting license-specific features.
- [Detach entitlements from a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-detach-entitlements): Use when removing license-specific features.
- [List license entitlements](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-list-entitlements): Use when inspecting features granted to a license.
- [Attach users to a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-attach-users): Use when allowing users to access a license.
- [Detach users from a license](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-detach-users): Use when removing user access from a license.
- [List license users](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-list-users): Use when auditing who can use a license.
- [Change license policy](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-change-policy): Use when moving a license to a different licensing model.
- [Change license owner](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-change-owner): Use when assigning a license to another user.
- [Change license group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/licenses/#licenses-relationships-change-group): Use when assigning a license to another group.

### Machines

Machines represent activated devices or instances. Use them for node-locked licensing, floating seats, fingerprints, heartbeats, and machine-level ownership.

- [Machines](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/): Overview of machine resources.
- [Machine object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-object): Use when reading machine fields and relationships.
- [Activate a machine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-create): Use when binding a license to a device fingerprint.
- [Retrieve a machine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-retrieve): Use when fetching one activation.
- [Update a machine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-update): Use when changing machine metadata.
- [Deactivate a machine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-delete): Use when removing an activation.
- [List all machines](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-list): Use when displaying or auditing activations.
- [Machine actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-actions): Use for machine checkout and heartbeat operations.
- [Check out machine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-actions-check-out): Use when generating a machine file certificate snapshot for offline or air-gapped licensing.
- [Ping machine heartbeat](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-actions-ping): Use when keeping a heartbeat-backed activation alive.
- [Reset machine heartbeat](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-actions-reset): Use when clearing heartbeat state.
- [Machine relationships](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-relationships): Use when managing machine associations.
- [Change machine owner](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-relationships-change-owner): Use when assigning a machine to another user.
- [Change machine group](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/machines/#machines-relationships-change-group): Use when assigning a machine to another group.

### Components

Components represent parts of a machine, such as hardware fingerprints. Use them when licensing needs component-level matching instead of a single fingerprint.

- [Components](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/): Overview of component resources.
- [Component object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-object): Use when reading component fields.
- [Add a component](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-create): Use when recording a machine component.
- [Retrieve a component](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-retrieve): Use when fetching one component.
- [Update a component](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-update): Use when changing component metadata.
- [Remove a component](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-delete): Use when removing a component from tracking.
- [List all components](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/components/#components-list): Use when displaying or auditing components.

### Processes

Processes represent running licensed instances. Use them for process tracking, heartbeat enforcement, and concurrency-limited licensing.

- [Processes](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/): Overview of process resources.
- [Process object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-object): Use when reading process fields.
- [Spawn a process](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-create): Use when starting to track a running process.
- [Retrieve a process](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-retrieve): Use when fetching one process.
- [Update a process](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-update): Use when changing process metadata.
- [Kill a process](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-delete): Use when ending process tracking.
- [List all processes](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-list): Use when displaying or auditing running processes.
- [Process actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-actions): Use for process operations.
- [Ping process heartbeat](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/processes/#processes-actions-ping): Use when keeping a tracked process alive.

## Distribution Resources

These resources model release distribution: packages, releases, artifacts, update feeds, engines, platforms, architectures, and channels.

### Auto-Updates

Auto-update docs explain how to connect Keygen distribution to common app update mechanisms.

- [Auto-updates](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/auto-updates/): Overview of auto-update integrations.
- [Go programs](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/auto-updates/#auto-updates-go): Use when updating Go binaries.
- [Tauri apps](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/auto-updates/#auto-updates-tauri): Use when configuring Tauri updates.
- [Electron apps](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/auto-updates/#auto-updates-electron): Use when configuring Electron updates.
- [Mac apps](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/auto-updates/#auto-updates-swift): Use when configuring native macOS updates.

### Engines

Engines expose distribution protocols for packages and update feeds. Use them to serve artifacts through ecosystem-specific clients.

- [Engines](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/): Overview of distribution engines.
- [Engine object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-object): Use when reading engine fields.
- [Retrieve an engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-retrieve): Use when fetching one engine.
- [List all engines](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-list): Use when discovering available engines.
- [Docker/OCI engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-oci): Use for private container registry distribution.
- [npm engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-npm): Use for private npm package distribution.
- [Rubygems engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-rubygems): Use for private Ruby gem distribution.
- [PyPI engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-pypi): Use for private Python package distribution.
- [Electron engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-electron): Use for Electron update feeds.
- [Tauri engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-tauri): Use for Tauri update feeds.
- [Raw engine](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-raw): Use for direct binary artifact distribution.

### Packages

Packages group releases for distribution. Use them when a product has versioned deliverables, modules, channels, or ecosystem-specific packages.

- [Packages](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/): Overview of package resources.
- [Package object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-object): Use when reading package fields.
- [Create a package](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-create): Use when adding a new distributable package.
- [Retrieve a package](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-retrieve): Use when fetching one package.
- [Update a package](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-update): Use when changing package metadata.
- [Delete a package](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-delete): Use when removing a package.
- [List all packages](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/packages/#packages-list): Use when displaying or auditing packages.

### Releases

Releases represent package versions. Use them to publish, yank, upgrade, constrain, and attach downloadable artifacts.

- [Releases](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/): Overview of release resources.
- [Release object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-object): Use when reading release fields.
- [Create a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-create): Use when creating a new version.
- [Retrieve a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-retrieve): Use when fetching one release.
- [Update a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-update): Use when changing release metadata.
- [Delete a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-delete): Use when removing a release.
- [List all releases](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-list): Use when displaying release history.
- [Upgrade a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-upgrade): Use when calculating or fetching an upgrade path.
- [Release actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-actions): Use for release lifecycle operations.
- [Publish a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-actions-publish): Use when making a release available.
- [Yank a release](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-actions-yank): Use when a release contains a bug or security issue.
- [Release relationships](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships): Use when managing release associations.
- [Download a release artifact](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships-retrieve-artifact): Use when downloading an artifact through a release.
- [List release artifacts](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships-list-artifacts): Use when showing files attached to a release.
- [Attach release constraints](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships-attach-constraints): Use when limiting release access by entitlement.
- [Detach release constraints](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships-detach-constraints): Use when removing entitlement-based release restrictions.
- [List release constraints](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/releases/#releases-relationships-list-constraints): Use when inspecting release access rules.

### Artifacts

Artifacts are downloadable files attached to releases. Use them for installers, binaries, archives, checksums, and protected downloads.

- [Artifacts](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/): Overview of artifact resources.
- [Artifact object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-object): Use when reading artifact fields.
- [Upload an artifact](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-create): Use when adding a downloadable file.
- [Download an artifact](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-retrieve): Use when retrieving a file.
- [Update an artifact](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-update): Use when changing artifact metadata.
- [Yank an artifact](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-delete): Use when withdrawing a file.
- [List all artifacts](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/artifacts/#artifacts-list): Use when displaying or auditing files.

### Platforms

Platforms describe target operating systems or runtimes. Use them to filter and target releases.

- [Platforms](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/platforms/): Overview of platform resources.
- [Platform object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/platforms/#platforms-object): Use when reading platform fields.
- [Retrieve a platform](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/platforms/#platforms-retrieve): Use when fetching one platform.
- [List all platforms](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/platforms/#platforms-list): Use when discovering supported platforms.

### Architectures

Architectures describe target CPU architectures. Use them with platforms and releases to serve the right artifact.

- [Architectures](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/arches/): Overview of architecture resources.
- [Architecture object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/arches/#arches-object): Use when reading architecture fields.
- [Retrieve an architecture](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/arches/#arches-retrieve): Use when fetching one architecture.
- [List all architectures](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/arches/#arches-list): Use when discovering supported architectures.

### Channels

Channels describe release tracks such as stable, beta, or edge. Use them to separate audiences and rollout paths.

- [Channels](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/channels/): Overview of channel resources.
- [Channel object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/channels/#channels-object): Use when reading channel fields.
- [Retrieve a channel](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/channels/#channels-retrieve): Use when fetching one channel.
- [List all channels](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/channels/#channels-list): Use when discovering available channels.

## Webhooks And Logs

These resources let external systems react to Keygen events and inspect operational history.

### Webhooks

Webhooks deliver Keygen events to external systems. Use them for billing sync, provisioning, audit trails, and retrying failed event delivery.

- [Webhooks](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/): Overview of webhook endpoints and events.
- [Webhook event types](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhooks-event-types): Use when choosing which events to subscribe to.
- [Webhook endpoint object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-object): Use when reading endpoint fields.
- [Create a webhook endpoint](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-create): Use when registering a receiver URL.
- [Retrieve a webhook endpoint](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-retrieve): Use when fetching one endpoint.
- [Update a webhook endpoint](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-update): Use when changing endpoint settings.
- [Delete a webhook endpoint](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-delete): Use when removing a receiver.
- [List webhook endpoints](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-endpoints-list): Use when displaying or auditing receivers.
- [Webhook event object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-object): Use when reading delivered event fields.
- [Retrieve a webhook event](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-retrieve): Use when inspecting one event.
- [Delete a webhook event](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-delete): Use when removing an event.
- [List webhook events](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-list): Use when displaying event history.
- [Webhook event actions](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-actions): Use for event operations.
- [Retry a webhook event](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/webhooks/#webhook-events-actions-retry): Use when redelivering a failed event.

### Request Logs

Request logs record API traffic. Use them to debug requests, inspect failures, and audit API usage.

- [Request logs](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/request-logs/): Overview of request log resources.
- [Request log object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/request-logs/#request-logs-object): Use when reading request log fields.
- [Retrieve a request log](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/request-logs/#request-logs-retrieve): Use when inspecting one API request.
- [List all request logs](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/request-logs/#request-logs-list): Use when reviewing API request history.

### Event Logs

Event logs record account activity. Use them for audit history, debugging resource changes, and operational observability.

- [Event logs](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/event-logs/): Overview of event log resources.
- [Event log object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/event-logs/#event-logs-object): Use when reading event log fields.
- [Retrieve an event log](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/event-logs/#event-logs-retrieve): Use when inspecting one account event.
- [List all event logs](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/event-logs/#event-logs-list): Use when reviewing account event history.

## Misc Resources

These resources cover profile lookup, password recovery, and second-factor authentication.

### Profiles

Profiles identify the current authenticated actor. Use them to answer "who am I?" for a token.

- [Profiles](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/profiles/): Overview of profile endpoints.
- [Who Am I?](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/profiles/#profiles-retrieve): Use when retrieving the current authenticated identity.

### Passwords

Password endpoints support account recovery. Use them when implementing forgot-password flows.

- [Passwords](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/passwords/): Overview of password recovery endpoints.
- [Forgot password](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/passwords/#passwords-forgot): Use when starting password recovery.

### Second Factors

Second factors add multi-factor authentication to users. Use them when managing MFA credentials.

- [Second factors](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors): Overview of second-factor resources.
- [Second factor object](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-object): Use when reading second-factor fields.
- [Create a second factor](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-create): Use when enrolling MFA.
- [Retrieve a second factor](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-retrieve): Use when fetching one MFA factor.
- [Update a second factor](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-update): Use when changing MFA metadata or state.
- [Delete a second factor](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-delete): Use when removing MFA.
- [List second factors](https://keygen.sh/docs/api/users/#second-factors-list): Use when displaying enrolled MFA factors.
